IMPORTANT: return the complete file in files (one entry with the whole new content), never edits. Rewrite docs/security-gate.md to match the code in your context after the review of the A1 follow-up; keep the structure and fix drift. It must state: every integration is gated (plain integrate runs the gate on the planned writes before its first write; because the dependency scanners read files from disk and plain integrate has no rollback, a change to a dependency manifest or lockfile (package.json, package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, requirements text files) is refused by plain integrate with "Use integrate --queue"; the queue audits the written files and rolls back; a gate that throws fails closed with security-gate-error and nothing is written); the default codeScan is local (NOT auto); the offline scan: 19 pinned rules (JavaScript, TypeScript, Python) in tools/security-rules/semgrep-local.yml with the sha256 pinned in the code, read once and copied into a fresh temp scan folder with a private HOME so a repo-written .semgrepignore or semgrep settings cannot change it, metrics off, version check off, a minimal environment with no tokens, no network; file names are compared case-insensitively (so PACKAGE.JSON and Cargo.TOML cannot slip through on macOS or Windows); new checks: policy-change (a batch that changes the security policy or sensitivity in .project-swarm.json is blocked: the owner makes that change by hand) and install-script (a changed lifecycle script in package.json: preinstall, install, postinstall, prepare, prepublish, prepublishOnly, prepack, postpack, preuninstall, uninstall, postuninstall); the unparsed list now also covers .npmrc, .yarnrc, .pnpmfile.cjs, bun and uv locks, setup.cfg, environment.yml, gradle wrapper and lockfile files, .gitmodules, CI workflows, vendored folders (vendor, third_party), .csproj and .gemspec files and requirements files inside a requirements folder or ending in .in or named constraints; allowUnparsedManifests matches exact paths (a bare name only at the repository root). Limits to state honestly: the registry checks, npm audit and osv-scanner send dependency names over the network even for sensitive projects; only the first 200 changed text files are code-scanned (a warning says so); the rules are a small starter set, not a full scanner.
